pages.name: Entering / Leaving a Jump
pages.html:
Entering Space / Leaving a Jump

Entering Space/Leaving a Jump: When a spacer leaves a spaceport and enters space or when they jump out of jumpspace, an encounter is rolled. Additional encounter checks will be made based on the location in space the spacer is currently located. See the following table to determine encounter check frequency.

  • Encounter check: Roll 1D and apply the Encounter Chance DM. On a result of 6+, there is an encounter. Roll 2D on the Space Encounter Type Table to determine what type of encounter it is.
  • Sensor operator: If an encounter occurs, the sensor operator makes a Routine Scan check. The effect of the roll over 6 determines how many range bands away the encounter is, up to the maximum range of the ship’s scanner. Any effect below 6+ is considered within close range of the spacer’s ship.
  • Please note: the sensor operator is scanning for all notable items. Ships are typically identified as such due to a heat signature from using the Maneuver Drive, while low-power ships that are drifting may read as space debris until they are investigated within close range.

Book p.80

pages.name: Space Encounter Procedure
pages.html:
Space Encounter Procedure

Space Encounter Procedure: Use the above table to determine when an encounter check is made based on where in space you’re currently located. This roll is modified by the Encounter Type DM column.

  • To make an encounter check: Roll 1D. A result of 6 is an encounter.
  • Determine encounter type: Roll 2D and consult the Encounter Type Table.
  • Number encountered: Roll the listed dice to determine how many encounters occur, to minimum of 1.

Book p.80

Space Ship Encounter Types:

  • Encounter: Encounters represent other spaceships discovered on the ship’s sensors that the spacers can interact with or ignore.
  • Encounter, Hostile: If an NPC is encountered, They will have -2 DM to interactions.
  • Encounter, Helpful: If an NPC is encountered, they will have +2 DM to interactions.
  • Environment: Environment encounters are situational scenarios dictated by the location the spacer is located, which provide a scenario that they may choose to interact with or, in some cases, one that they must deal with.

pages.name: Ship Communication and Scanning
pages.html:
Ship Communication

Ship Communication: The spacer can choose to use their comms to communicate to a ship or satellite they have detected. Use the Ship Encounter Reaction Table to determine their response.

Ship Scanning

Ship Scanning: The sensor operator may choose to scan ships they have detected to gather more information about them without directly communicating, if they have the necessary equipment.

  • Military-grade sensors can access the legal status of the ship, using the ship's computer and library to determine the ship’s and owner’s history. This may also be accessible to a spacer if they have been given access to similar data from a patron or due to their connections.
  • Actively scanning a ship will alert the pilot and sensor operator that they are being scanned, incurring a -3DM to the reaction and behaviour columns on the table below.

Book p.82

Ship Encounter Reaction Table: Use the following table when attempting to contact a ship over the comms or when scanning it.

12+HelpfulEvasiveNo issue, and no record of any delinquencyAppears new or recently upgraded

If the ship is flagged, roll 1D to determine the complication:

  • 1) Unregistered or false registration; escort to closest starport for a reward
  • 2) Ship is registered to someone else
  • 3) Skipped on ship loan payments; reward available if detained
  • 4) Sensors picked up mysterious cargo
  • 5) Owner is affiliated with an enemy government, faction, or criminal enterprise; reward available
  • 6) Ship is legendary or notorious; proceed with caution
